transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for hopping on, we know this is procurement heavy so we'll try to keep it structured. Jordan from Redwood, joined by Priya our solutions engineer and Marcus from CSM.
[00:10] Samantha Ortiz: Hi, Sam here. Thanks. We're expecting to move quickly on this if we can finalize legal and pricing this week.
[00:18] Priya Shah: Hi Sam, thanks. Quick note, I'm going to cover the security artifacts and the pilot runbook after Jordan walks through the contract items.
[00:26] Dr. Amit Verma: Amit here, I'll be listening for the technical constraints - VPC, KMS, and any private deployment options.
[00:33] Lena Park: Lena from legal. We'll flag a few standard MSA/DPA items - liability cap, indemnity, data retention, and breach notification timelines.
[00:40] Jordan Lee: Great. First on the MSA, the redline we sent had the standard 12 month term and a 6 month notice for termination; you had proposed a 90 day notice, iirc?
[00:50] Samantha Ortiz: Yeah we usually ask for 90 day notice on these enterprise contracts. Also parity on liability cap with our platform vendors.
[00:59] Marcus Nguyen: One ask we commonly see is a clause for service credits tied to SLA breaches rather than termination rights. We can be flexible there.
[01:08] Lena Park: For us the primary issue is the cap and the carve-outs for gross negligence - we need clarity.
[01:14] Jordan Lee: Understood. We can propose a middle ground on cap and keep gross negligence carve-out as is; Priya, can you confirm our standard liability language?
[01:22] Priya Shah: Yes our standard is 3x monthly fees or $1M whichever is greater, with carve-outs for willful misconduct. We can, uh, discuss higher caps for an enterprise SOW.
[01:31] Lena Park: We'll push back to parity but okay for initial pilot.
[01:35] Carlos Reyes: On security, two big items - KMS integration for customer-managed keys and log retention. We need assurance that logs containing sensitive PII can be retained within our AWS region.
[01:45] Priya Shah: For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and regional data residency. For our hosted API the data plane is in us-west-2 and we offer optional VPC peering for dedicated customers.
[01:56] Maya Singh: Can you confirm whether the KV cache or prefix cache persists customer data and for how long?
[02:01] Priya Shah: Good question - KV cache is ephemeral per-instance to support response generation; we don't persist it beyond the session for hosted mode. For caching options you can choose persistent caching on Redwood Dedicated, but it's encrypted and configurable for retention.
[02:16] Dr. Amit Verma: We need a formal note for the DPA about sub-processors - do you have an up-to-date list and a notification process for changes?
[02:24] Jordan Lee: Yes we'll share our sub-processor list and we notify customers 30 days in advance for any changes that materially affect data processing. It's in the DPA appendix.
[02:33] Lena Park: On breach notification we require 72 hours. What's your standard?
[02:37] Priya Shah: We aim for 72 hours, SOC2 controls align with that; our incident response playbook supports 72 hour notifications.
[02:44] Samantha Ortiz: Pricing - procurement wants a pilot credit and a predictable unit price for the pilot. We need numbers to route for approval.
[02:52] Marcus Nguyen: For pilots we typically provide a discounted rate or credits. Marcus will prepare a pricing worksheet and pilot invoice - can you share expected token/throughput for the pilot Maya?
[03:02] Maya Singh: Expecting ~200k requests over two weeks, mixed embed and generation traffic, median prompt length ~120 tokens.
[03:10] Marcus Nguyen: Great, that helps. We'll model cost and propose a credit amount.
[03:15] Jordan Lee: On SLAs - you flagged latency SLOs vs cost. For Redwood Dedicated we can commit to p95 latency targets plus an availability SLA of 99.9% for reserved capacity. For hosted API, we provide best-effort but can tier up with reserved pools.
[03:29] Dr. Amit Verma: Is uptime measured per region or per deployment id? We need region-level guarantees.
[03:34] Priya Shah: We measure availability per deployment/cluster; for customers requiring region residency and SLA we recommend Dedicated in that region.
[03:41] Carlos Reyes: Encryption in transit and at rest - do you support customer-managed keys for both logs and model artifacts?
[03:48] Priya Shah: We support CMK for data-at-rest on Dedicated; model artifacts for hosted are stored in our encrypted buckets with provider-managed keys, but for Private we can configure CMK. We'll document that in the compliance pack.
[03:59] Lena Park: Liability and indemnity - two specific asks: 1) carve out for regulated data if you operate in a private deployment vs hosted; 2) we want a mutual indemnity for third party claims arising from data.
[04:10] Jordan Lee: We'll ask legal to prepare language for mutual indemnity; for regulated data we recommend Private deployment, which is a separate commercial term.
[04:18] Samantha Ortiz: What's the expected timeline if we approve the pilot - how quickly can onboarding and a technical kickoff happen?
[04:23] Marcus Nguyen: We can do a technical kickoff within one week of signed pilot SOW; typical onboarding for a basic pilot is 2-3 business days of setup plus an initial observation period.
[04:33] Maya Singh: For the pilot we need an architecture diagram and the pre-signed certs for the VPC peering.
[04:38] Priya Shah: We'll share the architecture diagram and a VPC peering checklist.
[04:42] Jordan Lee: Ok next steps: we'll send redlined MSA and DPA, SOC2 artifacts, pricing worksheet. Lena, can you confirm availability for a 30 minute legal review on Tuesday?
[04:52] Lena Park: Tuesday 10am works.
[04:55] Jordan Lee: Great, we'll put that on calendar. Anything else from NovusCare?
[05:00] Samantha Ortiz: One quick thing - can we get a list of your sub-processors and the contact for security questions?
[05:06] Priya Shah: Yes I'll include the sub-processor list and our security contact (sec-questions@redwood.ai) in the packet.
[05:12] Dr. Amit Verma: Also would like an optional benchmark run - small latency benchmark against our expected workload.
[05:17] Jordan Lee: We can run a scoped benchmark for the pilot; Marcus will include that in the runbook.
[05:21] Samantha Ortiz: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[05:23] Jordan Lee: Thanks - we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[05:27] (crosstalk) Lena Park: Thanks.
[05:30] End of recording. Note: transcription contains occasional proper noun errors (eg Redwood spelled Redwood Infference) and timestamps approximate.
